source_role: AIGMos Build Tool source and provenance policy, not canonical CW Ruleset

confirmed.rule: Pruning starts from a complete source-system checkout/inventory loaded together, not independently downloaded module versions.
Do NOT create a per-dependency version-resolution requirement for Build Tool. Direct deps/libs use unambiguous identifiers from one source snapshot.
Record provenance at whole-source-snapshot level (e.g. Git commit/source tree digest) for reproducible/traced output.
Build Tool forms dependency closure from direct source headers, selected components, source registry and declared resources; only required code is included.
Build profiles store selected composition; the generated artifact stores actual source hashes, selected graph and validation/provenance.

pipeline: Inventory files, registered module identities, source headers and CodeMarkup metadata
Validate single-snapshot identifiers and declared direct dependencies
Resolve closure using local snapshot only; missing required dependency => FAIL
Select target-specific code and remove unselected features physically
Validate generated source, imports, CS/TER references and target compatibility
Emit source provenance and artifact report, then test/provision/deploy as separately specified

separation.build_profile: Reusable user-chosen selection; MAY pin full source snapshot for repeatability.
separation.source_snapshot: Coherent imported set of source code, metadata, module manifests and resources; source provenance ID/hash.
separation.dependency_graph: Calculated from snapshot declarations and selected profile, never a manually maintained version solver.
separation.artifact: Generated target-specific source and validation/provenance, excluding secrets and unselected code.

non_requirements: Per-module semantic-version constraints solely for pruning
Per-dependency version selectors and lockfile solving across remote registries
Independent network fetching or mixed-revision dependency assembly as part of basic Build Tool
hard_gates: Missing required file/module/library in full source snapshot => FAIL; no automatic remote downloads
Source selected for MP contains unsupported CP-only unresolved references => FAIL
Nondeterminism from different source snapshots must not be concealed; record snapshot identity
Snapshot provenance and per-emitted-file source mapping must be traceable
notes: Snapshot-level version information does not mean all source must share the same individual file version number; provenance establishes exactly which files formed the input.
Third-party library versions, if present in source, may be recorded as factual provenance but the Builder does not need to invent a per-dependency version negotiation system.
The source-header v0.2.0 target semantic migration remains a separate unlocked contract change.
Module metadata and policy validation remain necessary; absence of version solving does not waive dependency correctness or external library safety.
open: Exact snapshot ID/hash representation, Git vs archive vs working tree provenance
How to refuse or warn about a dirty checkout when reproducibility requested
Whether selected third-party libraries are expected to be vendored in snapshot or can be declared as target-owned system facilities
Which source-hash/canonicalization strategy is stable across hosts
